title: Seatless commit collars and scheduled upgrade policy for private/VPC & on-prem deployments
creator: Elena Park
description: Context: Enterprise customers buying Redwood Private/VPC frequently request non-seat-based pricing, predictable upgrade windows, and flexible support SLAs. This ticket defines and pilots a set of 'seatless commit collars' (capacity/commit bands that are not per-user), a modular support tier matrix for on-prem customers, and a scheduled upgrade cadence policy with LTS/patch options for regulated customers. Goal: propose an experiment we can offer to 6 pilot customers and measure conversion, churn risk, and lift in ACV.
acceptance_criteria: Pricing experiment proposal doc reviewed and approved by Sales, Finance, Legal, and Security
Three distinct commit bands defined with example pricing and unit economics (margins, payback)
Support tier definitions (Standard, Premium, Enterprise) complete with SLOs, response windows, and escalation paths
Upgrade cadence policy options (Quarterly managed updates, Biannual LTS, Emergency patching) drafted and validated with Engineering and Security
Pilot enrollment playbook and templated contract language created for 6 customers
Tracking dashboard requirements specified (conversion rate, MRR/ACV impact, time-to-upgrade, support tickets per-month)
Security review sign-off appended to ticket (if required)
proposed_pricing_matrix: Band A (Small commit): 8-32 reserved GPU hours / month => base license fee $12k/month + $0.18 per reserved GPU-hour above band
Band B (Mid commit): 33-128 reserved GPU hours / month => base license fee $40k/month + $0.12 per reserved GPU-hour above band
Band C (Large commit): 129+ reserved GPU hours / month => base license fee $120k/month + negotiated overage rate
Optional add-ons: High-availability cluster licensing (+20% of base), Offline airgap packaging (one-time $25k), Migration credit (up to 3 months free for 12-month commits)
support_tier_definitions: Standard: Business hours support (M-F 9am-5pm local), 24-48h response for Sev2, included in base license
Premium: 24/7 support, 4h response for Sev1, proactive monthly health checks, phone escalation, +15% of base license
Enterprise (SLA): 24/7 priority with 1h response for Sev1, dedicated TAM, quarterly onsite/remote architecture reviews, customizable runbooks, +30% of base license or fixed retainer
upgrade_cadence_options: Managed Quarterly: default for most customers; smaller, controlled feature releases every quarter with opt-in for early access
Biannual LTS: large upgrades provided twice per year with 18-month security support window (recommended for regulated customers)
Emergency Patch Window: out-of-band security fixes applied within 72 hours for all paid tiers; Enterprise customers get 24h target
Opt-out and self-managed: customers may choose to self-manage upgrades for a discount; Redwood provides signed binaries and onboarding support but no upgrade guarantees
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: Complete internal review (Sales, Legal, Finance, Security, Eng) and update pricing model spreadsheets
Week 3-4: Recruit 4-6 pilot customers via account execs; prepare pilot contracts and MSA addendum templates
Month 2: Deploy experiment offers, instrument billing and telemetry, surface pilot offers in Console as 'Private pilot' option
Month 3-6: Observe pilot, hold monthly check-ins, collect metrics and qualitative feedback, iterate pricing and SLA wording
Month 6: Decision gate - scale to GA, continue A/B testing, or retire. Present results to GTM and Exec
metrics_and_okrs: Primary: Pilot conversion rate to paid commit within 90 days >= 50%
Revenue: Incremental ARR from pilots >= $400k annualized by month 6
Operational: Mean time to upgrade for pilot customers <= target (Quarterly <= 7 days; LTS <= 21 days)
Support: Ticket volume per customer does not increase > 20% vs baseline after adoption
Retention: 12-month churn for pilot cohort <= baseline enterprise churn

Risk: Upgrade cadence complexity increases support load—monitor ticket spikes closely during rollout
